title: Bittensor Daily News — October 31, 2026
summary: REAX owner stake lock verified after its allocation change; Ditto announces memory encryption at rest; Desearch opens a scholarship-search example. Also: Reliquary’s distributed-RL report, a developing Perturb wallet incident, miner rule changes, EveryFrame tools and NOAH’s planned research votes.

ecosystem.headline: Const frames neutral AI as a strategic crypto use case
ecosystem.summary: In October 30 commentary, Const contrasts fiat AI with Bitcoin AI and discusses Cohere’s Canada investment plans as geopolitical context. This is a view about neutral AI infrastructure, not evidence of a new Bittensor partnership, funding commitment or protocol activation. In a related reply he describes SN75 Hippius’s CDN, compute, storage and networking ambitions; this is commentary, not a new independent Cloudflare-comparison benchmark.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Relevant founder commentary clearly distinguished from execution.

ecosystem.headline: Latest Shizzy market episode is in the public library
ecosystem.summary: The October 30 market episode is public and now appears in the website video library. It contains the 10 to 100 TAO challenge update and dated market commentary. TAO Templar remains a completed replay; Leadpoet remains an upcoming November 5 stream. Upcoming broadcasts are excluded from the default recent-video player.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Original Shizzy coverage with completed and upcoming status separated.

updates.headline: SN22 Desearch publishes an open Scholarship Finder example
updates.summary: The October 31 announcement links a public Python example that turns field, study level and year into a deadline-sorted shortlist with source URLs. Its repository dates the code to October 30 and documents date-confidence flags, extraction failures and the need to check the official scholarship page. The code and sample exist; eligibility, deadline correctness and paid API execution were not independently tested.
updates.ratingReason: An inspectable developer example with useful provenance and clear output limitations.

updates.headline: SN26 Perturb: public brief reports team-wallet compromise
updates.summary: The October 31 dated public brief attributes a wallet-compromise announcement to the team and says it delayed a planned product release while investigating. The linked Discord original required login during review. No verified loss amount, attack cause, affected address list or recovery deadline is available in this report. This remains a developing safety lead, not an independently reconstructed incident.
updates.ratingReason: Potentially material safety information warrants coverage with the primary-access gap prominent.

updates.headline: SN44 Score reports block removals and unavailable tracks
updates.summary: The October 31 brief reports removal of misannotated PPE, room-dirtiness and petrol-station blocks, two Football private-track exclusions after spot-check failures, and unavailable fallen-person and beverage tracks. These affect scoring and participation. The original private messages and fixes were not independently verified; no wallet-person attribution is made.
updates.ratingReason: Scoring reliability and participation changes merit attributed operational coverage.

updates.headline: SN50 Synth: response-time rules planned for November 2
updates.summary: The October 31 public brief says Synth Ultra will count a prediction over 10 ms as a miss and stop rewards when the 24-hour mean exceeds 5 ms, effective November 2 at 00:00 UTC. It also reports a seven-day prompt dataset for miners. These are attributed operational rules with a future effective boundary; the Discord original and activation were not independently inspected.
updates.ratingReason: Actionable miner requirements, with timing and secondary-source status explicit.

updates.headline: SN53 engy: 5,568.586960919 alpha transaction burn carry-forward
updates.summary: The October 30 successful transaction burn at block 9398416 destroyed 5,568.586960919 SN53 alpha. This is a dated carry-forward of the already archived event, not an additional burn. Native alpha amount is distinct from TAO spent, fees or withheld miner emissions; execution alone does not establish the revenue source.
updates.ratingReason: A qualifying successful explicit transaction burn with permanent evidence.

updates.headline: SN60 Bitsec: hidden-project endpoint remains unresolved
updates.summary: The October 31 brief says the team is selecting seven random projects immediately before evaluation to make hardsteering harder while the hidden-project endpoint remains unfixed. This is an attributed mitigation and unresolved evaluation-integrity issue, not a verified completed endpoint repair.
updates.ratingReason: Useful miner warning with the remaining limitation clear.

updates.headline: SN68 NOVA: finalized 26/41/33 allocation carry-forward
updates.summary: Dated carry-forward: at block 9398764 (2026-10-30T19:32:36+00:00), owner allocation changed 18% to 26%, validators stayed 41%, miners changed 41% to 33%; TAO/recycle slots remained zero. Exact raw five-slot vectors and successful execution remain in the permanent archive. This is the same previously archived event, not another change today. Root baseline is paid first, capped by the validator share; historical yields can lag. A split change alone does not prove stake-lock deposits.
updates.ratingReason: Verified material allocation change carried into the full morning edition with its actual event date.

updates.headline: SN78 Umi plans an execution-efficiency modifier for C8
updates.summary: The October 31 brief describes 16 challenges per model in the current round and a planned roughly 15% execution-speed reward modifier for C8, with details forthcoming. Repository discovery includes quality-gated CPU-efficiency reward code. Neither the approximate modifier nor code discovery proves final live parameters.
updates.ratingReason: Forward miner-planning information; final rules and activation remain unverified.

updates.headline: SN79 MVTRX: brief reports v0.6.6 mainnet rollout
updates.summary: The October 31 brief reports v0.6.6 on mainnet with simulation balances carried over, skill-mark and maker-fill-only credit phased over three simulated hours. Refined markets are planned for November 3. Miners are directed to update; live scoring execution was not independently tested.
updates.ratingReason: Specific operator consequences without treating a future market run as completed.

updates.headline: SN81 Reliquary reports a 100-step distributed reinforcement-learning run
updates.summary: October 31 the team amplified a contributor report of 100 steps using rollouts from untrusted miners across 12+ GPU models, with public sampling-noise controls and on-subnet evaluation checks. The attached chart was inspected; the run and chart scores were not independently reproduced. Separately, merged PR 434 fixes evaluation retries so a failed slot retains its draw and every drawn position is judged. A code merge does not by itself prove deployment or the headline run’s results.
updates.ratingReason: Substantive first-party research and evaluation work, bounded by the lack of independent reproduction.

updates.headline: SN82 NOAH plans miner research and holder votes
updates.summary: The October 30 Eastern / October 31 UTC original and graphic say Coming soon: miners analyze subnets, holders review reports and vote on subnet-token purchases funded by a portion of owner emissions. Purchases would be held as permanent capital according to the team. No voting launch date, completed purchase or implementation of permanence was verified. The separate emission-disable alert remains a distinct verification lead.
updates.ratingReason: A specific governance and capital-allocation plan with execution left pending.

updates.headline: SN91 Cascade announces its mixture-of-experts competition live
updates.summary: Late-found October 30 announcement at 13:43 UTC: the team says submissions are open for training a 1.23B time-series foundation model, with Timestral-209M as a comparison baseline. The launch announcement adds information beyond yesterday’s code-merge coverage. No completed training win, independent benchmark result or live submission was tested. The short launch video was sampled visually; full audio was not reviewed.
updates.ratingReason: A first-party participation announcement with launch and performance claims separated.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX: owner locks 230.554726488 alpha in a successful transaction
updates.summary: Finalized block 9403214 on October 31 at 10:22:36 UTC contains a successful lock_stake call by the current SN92 owner: 230.554726488 alpha, extrinsic 14/event 248, registration 9247819. This independently confirms one deposit after the October 30 allocation change, rather than only a promise. It does not establish daily recurrence, the exact release schedule or that every extra owner-emission payment has been locked. Locked stake is not destroyed supply.
updates.ratingReason: Direct execution resolves an important verification gap, with the scope limited to one deposit.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX: finalized 26/41/33 allocation carry-forward
updates.summary: Dated carry-forward: at block 9399960 (2026-10-30T23:31:48+00:00), owner allocation changed 18% to 26%, validators stayed 41%, miners changed 41% to 33%; TAO/recycle slots remained zero. Exact raw five-slot vectors and successful execution remain in the permanent archive. This is the same previously archived event, not another change today. Root baseline is paid first, capped by the validator share; historical yields can lag. A split change alone does not prove stake-lock deposits.
updates.ratingReason: Verified material allocation change carried into the full morning edition with its actual event date.

updates.headline: SN107 Minos: release date and split still forthcoming
updates.summary: The October 31 brief says four app updates shipped after limited-user testing, with few bugs remaining. A mainnet release date and emission split are promised soon; neither is announced as a completed launch here.
updates.ratingReason: A useful development-stage update, not a mainnet launch claim.

updates.headline: SN117 EveryFrame adds eleven Director tools
updates.summary: October 30 EveryFrame announced eleven additions, including Kling 4.0 Edit, H3 Max Recast/Relight, FLUX Klein LoRA, Motion-to-Code, VEED Dubbing and HeyGen Voice. The public Director catalog and selected release-video frames were inspected in the dated monitor. This broadens the visible creative tool selection; model quality, lowest-price claims and paid usage were not independently tested.
updates.ratingReason: A concrete product-catalog expansion retained from the after-cutoff queue.

updates.headline: SN118 Ditto announces encryption for stored memories and search data
updates.summary: The October 31 original introduces a passphrase flow for encrypting a selected memory group and its search data. Ditto explicitly calls this encryption at rest: it still reads memories when answering. Users are told to save a recovery kit. This is a useful storage-privacy control, not a claim of end-to-end protection from the assistant; no cryptographic audit or account mutation was performed.
updates.ratingReason: A concrete product control with its security boundary stated accurately.

updates.headline: SN124 Swarm: evaluation queues remain a miner concern
updates.summary: The October 31 public brief contains member reports of slow queues and a claimed increase from roughly 278 to 537 seeds/hour, alongside proposals for early rejection and more concurrency. It explicitly has no confirmed team post. These figures are community observations, not verified recovery, a promised service level or team-reported adoption.
updates.ratingReason: An unresolved operator issue with attribution separated from measurement.
